hardFacts: Nick Bosa returns Sunday vs. Las Vegas for the first time since Week 2 without a restrictive game designation after clearing post-Bye full-speed pass-rush reps.
Christian McCaffrey exited the Week 8 Bye off the injury report and is a full go for Sunday at Levi's Stadium (1:25 PM PT, FOX).

Week 9 marks the first snap sequence under DC Raheem Morris pairing Nick Bosa and Keion White (3.5 sacks) on the edges with newly re-acquired DeForest Buckner (4.0 sacks, 8 QB hits) and Osa Odighizuwa (#92, 2.0 sacks, 7 QB hits) at 3-tech / 2i interior alignments.
schemeAndCapTakeaways: Pass-Rush Stunt Geometry: Having both Buckner (6'7", 34.4" arms) and Odighizuwa inside keeps Mykel Williams on the edge full-time and forces opposing protections to slide interior help, isolating Bosa 1-on-1 on the Wide-9 rail without needing 5-man pressures.

Run-Fit Impact vs. Raiders Outside Zone: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak runs heavy wide-zone/boot action with Kirk Cousins, Ashton Jeanty, and Brock Bowers; Buckner's vertical knock-back disrupts playside combo climbs to Fred Warner.
clusteredBriefs.consensusVsDissent: Unanimous beat consensus that SF will still manage Bosa around 42–48 snaps (~68% share) in his first game back, rotating Keion White, Romello Height, and Mykel Williams across early run downs and speed-rush situations.

Brandon Aiyuk Contract & Cap Breakdown — OverTheCap

hardFacts: Brandon Aiyuk and agent Drew Rosenhaus met with 49ers leadership at SAP Performance Facility on Friday, Nov 6, stating he is physically healthy and seeking reinstatement; NFL Network notes ~$13M in bonus forfeiture complicates a simple release.

With Aiyuk (Personal), Mike Evans (27 rec, 420 yds, +40.9 EPA — Out, Achilles), Deebo Samuel Sr. (16 rec, 206 yds — Out, Hamstring), and Christian Kirk (Knee - Meniscus) ruled Out—and Ricky Pearsall + rookie De'Zhaun Stribling on IR—Kyle Shanahan signaled Demarcus Robinson (Questionable, Ankle) is likely to be activated from IR.

Under OverTheCap's 2026 ledger ($35.16M gross cap space vs. -$31.54M projected in 2027), any Post-June 1 trade or release keeps current-year proration on 2026 while deferring remaining future bonus acceleration into 2027.
schemeAndCapTakeaways: Cap Math Reality: Because prorated signing/option bonus acceleration after June 1 splits remaining future-year proration into 2027 dead money, resolving Aiyuk's contract preserves 2026 cap room ($35.16M) for CBA Article 13 rollover into 2027.

On-Field Week 9 WR Rotation: Jordan Watkins (6/9, 138 yds), Brandin Cooks (#84), Jacob Cowing (#4), and likely IR-activation Demarcus Robinson handle 11-personnel WR snaps alongside high-volume 21/12-personnel focal points George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey.
clusteredBriefs.consensusVsDissent: National insiders (Schefter/Pelissero/Maiocco/Barrows) note Friday's NFL personnel notice included no immediate reinstatement, pointing toward a structured trade or settlement rather than immediate snap reintegration.

San Francisco 49ers 2026–2030 Salary Cap Table — OverTheCap

hardFacts: The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline arrives Tuesday, Nov 10 at 1:00 PM PT (4:00 PM ET).

After sending their 2027 4th-round pick to Indianapolis for DT DeForest Buckner ($7.90M 2026 cap charge absorbed from ~$41.26M pre-Buckner room), John Lynch & Paraag Marathe hold $35.16M in gross 2026 cap space (#1 in NFC) and 6 remaining 2027 draft picks (Rd 1, 2, 3, 5, 6-BAL, 7-KC).

With six receivers unavailable (Evans, Samuel, Kirk, Pearsall, Stribling, Aiyuk) and NFC West rival Seattle acquiring All-Pro LG Quenton Nelson, front office calls prioritize WR/pass-catching 12-personnel TE, Left Guard pass protection (Connor Colby pressure spike), and expiring Edge rentals.
schemeAndCapTakeaways: Purchasing-Power Leverage (9/18ths Proration): With 9 weeks elapsed in an 18-week season, SF can absorb 50% (9/18ths) of an incoming rental's 2026 base salary directly—keeping pick costs down to Day 3 rather than paying sellers to eat cash.

2027 Cap Deficit Constraint (-$31.54M Projected): Because OverTheCap projects San Francisco at -$31.54M in 2027 on an estimated $327M ceiling, unused 2026 cap rolls over 1-for-1 under CBA Article 13—making expiring 2026 rentals ($0 in 2027) or cheap rookie deals strongly preferred over multi-year veteran guarantees.
clusteredBriefs.consensusVsDissent: Beat & national insiders (Schefter, Rapoport, Barrows, Maiocco) expect SF to pursue Day-3 expiring rentals or rookie-scale fits (Adonai Mitchell, Josh Downs, Rashod Bateman, Greg Dulcich, or Khalil Mack) while protecting 2027 Round 1–3 picks.
